entities.title: The git tag is the only source of version numbers
entities.summary: The repository's crates and the indexer say 0.0.0-dev; a release takes its version from its vX.Y.Z tag and stamps it into every binary at build time.
entities.context: Every tool ships in one release, and its --version should report that release.
entities.decision: version.sh takes a pushed vX.Y.Z tag as it is, or computes the next version after the latest vX.Y.Z tag for a manual run's bump (patch, minor or major; none only builds), and the run tags the commit itself. set-version.sh writes that version into every crate's manifest and Cargo.lock entry without resolving anything, so --locked still holds, and the indexer is published with -p:Version. Releases are created with no release notes.

entities.title: Pour a bottle instead of building from source
entities.summary: The formula carries a bottle block, so brew install pours the prebuilt binaries and skips Homebrew's build-from-source checks.
entities.context: Homebrew's build-from-source path demands up-to-date Command Line Tools, though the formula only copies prebuilt binaries.
entities.decision: bottle.sh packs one bottle, tagged all because the binaries are universal and the formula macOS-only; the release job uploads it to the GitHub release and formula.sh points the formula's bottle block there. The release tarball stays the formula's source fallback.
entities.rationale: Installs succeed without current Command Line Tools.

entities.title: One formula for every tool, at the release's version
entities.summary: A single zazzle formula installs zazzle, zazzled, afs, fix-network, free-disk-space and zazzle-csharp-indexer, and takes the release tag as its version.
entities.context: Every tool ships in one tarball from one tag.
entities.decision: formula.sh writes Formula/zazzle.rb, installing all the binaries and versioned with the tag without its v.
entities.rationale: Every release is an upgrade, and one brew install gives every tool.

entities.title: Ship the C# indexer gzipped per CPU type and expand it after install
entities.summary: zazzle-csharp-indexer is a self-contained single file per CPU type, so the tarball and bottle hold both gzipped and the formula's post_install_steps expands the one for the Mac over a placeholder.
entities.context: The other binaries are universal; the .NET single-file publish is not, and the formula and bottle are tagged all.
entities.decision: The release publishes osx-arm64 and osx-x64 and gzips each into the tarball; the formula installs both into libexec/indexer and a placeholder bin/zazzle-csharp-indexer that brew links, and post_install_steps replaces the placeholder with the file for uname -m. brew postinstall zazzle reruns it.

entities.title: Publish the formula to the zazzcat/homebrew-z tap
entities.summary: The release pushes Formula/zazzle.rb to the external tap repository zazzcat/homebrew-z with a fine-grained token, instead of committing formulas to this repository.
entities.context: brew taps a repository named homebrew-<tap> by itself, so brew install zazzcat/z/zazzle works without a separate tap command; GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push to another account's repository.
entities.decision: The homebrew job checks out zazzcat/homebrew-z with HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN (Contents: read and write on that repository only), writes the formula there and pushes to its default branch.

entities.title: Profile-guided optimization for zazzled's C code only
entities.summary: The release compiles tree-sitter's C code in zazzled with a clang profile trained on crate sources; the Rust code is not profiled.
entities.context: Tree-sitter's C code dominates parsing. Rust's own PGO needs an llvm-profdata that matches rustc's LLVM, which Xcode's tools do not guarantee.
entities.decision: pgo.sh builds an instrumented zazzled for the host target only, trains it with outline and refs over the cargo registry sources, merges the profile with the toolchain's llvm-profdata and prints PGO_CFLAGS; the release builds with CC=clang and those flags, and on macOS the arm64 profile also serves the x86_64 slice.

entities.title: Signing and notarization are optional
entities.summary: The release signs and notarizes the macOS binaries only when the Apple secrets are set, and otherwise releases them unsigned with a warning.
entities.context: Only browser downloads need a signature: Homebrew does not quarantine what a formula installs, and a file downloaded with curl runs as is.
entities.decision: sign-and-notarize.sh skips with a warning when a secret is missing, unless the repository variable REQUIRE_SIGNING is true, where it fails the release.
